_about: The kingdom side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of God's reign and kingdom that more than one book shares, from the Law and the Psalms to Daniel, the Gospels and Revelation, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: The LORD reigns

The Law & history: Let them say among the nations
Psalms & wisdom: The LORD reigns! He is robed in majesty
The LORD reigns, let the earth rejoice
The LORD reigns; let the nations tremble!
God reigns over the nations; God is seated on His holy throne
The LORD reigns forever, your God, O Zion
Revelation: You have taken Your great power and have begun to reign
Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns

rows.alike: Each but Revelation 11:17 says in the present tense that God reigns: "The LORD reigns" (1 Chronicles 16:31; Psalms 93:1, 96:10, 97:1, 99:1), "The LORD reigns forever" (Psalm 146:10), "God reigns over the nations" (Psalm 47:8), "Your God reigns!" (Isaiah 52:7), "the Lord our God the Almighty reigns" (Revelation 19:6).
rows.different: 1 Chronicles 16:31 and Psalm 96:10 give it as words to be said "among the nations"; Isaiah 52:7 has it said "to Zion" by those "who bring good news", and Psalm 146:10 says "your God, O Zion"; Psalm 97:1 adds "let the earth rejoice" and Psalm 99:1 "let the nations tremble!". In Revelation it is thanks to "Lord God Almighty" who has "begun to reign" (11:17) and the cry of "a great multitude" beginning "Hallelujah!" (19:6).

rows.title: The LORD will reign forever; the eternal King

The Law & history: The LORD will reign forever and ever!
Psalms & wisdom: The LORD is King forever and ever
the LORD is enthroned as King forever
The LORD reigns forever, your God, O Zion, for all generations
He rules forever by His power
The Prophets: He is the living God and eternal King
The letters: 1 Timothy 1:17
Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God

rows.alike: Each joins God's reign or kingship to "forever": "The LORD will reign forever and ever!" (Exodus 15:18), "The LORD is King forever and ever" (Psalm 10:16), "You, O LORD, reign forever" (Lamentations 5:19); Jeremiah 10:10 has "eternal King" and 1 Timothy 1:17 "the King eternal".
rows.different: Exodus 15:18 says "will reign", Psalm 10:16 "is King" and Psalm 146:10 "reigns"; Psalm 10:16 goes on "the nations perish from His land", Psalm 29:10 has Him "enthroned over the flood", and Psalm 146:10 adds "your God, O Zion, for all generations". Jeremiah 10:10 adds "The earth quakes at His wrath"; 1 Timothy 1:17 adds "immortal, and invisible, the only God" and ends in a doxology, "be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen."

rows.title: An everlasting kingdom, from generation to generation

Psalms & wisdom: Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and Your dominion endures through all generations
The Prophets: His kingdom is an eternal kingdom; His dominion endures from generation to generation
His dominion is an everlasting dominion, and His kingdom endures from generation to generation
His kingdom will never be destroyed, and His dominion will never end
the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed
The letters: 2 Peter 1:11
the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ

rows.alike: Psalm 145:13 and Daniel 4:3 and 4:34 pair "kingdom" with "dominion" in nearly the same words: "Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and Your dominion endures through all generations", "His kingdom is an eternal kingdom; His dominion endures from generation to generation". Daniel 2:44 and 6:26 both have "will never be destroyed", and 2 Peter 1:11 has "the eternal kingdom".
rows.different: Psalm 145 speaks to God ("Your kingdom"); in Daniel 4:3 and 4:34 the words are King Nebuchadnezzar's, and in 6:26 King Darius's decree; in Daniel 2:44 Daniel says "the God of heaven will set up a kingdom" "In the days of those kings" that "will shatter all these kingdoms". 2 Peter 1:11 names it "the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ" and speaks of "a lavish reception into" it.

rows.title: The kingdom belongs to the LORD

The Law & history: Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom, and You are exalted as head over all
Psalms & wisdom: For dominion belongs to the LORD
The Prophets: And the kingdom will belong to the LORD.

rows.alike: Each says the kingdom or dominion is the LORD's: "Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom" (1 Chronicles 29:11), "dominion belongs to the LORD" (Psalm 22:28), "the kingdom will belong to the LORD" (Obadiah 1:21).
rows.different: 1 Chronicles 29:11 is David speaking to the LORD before all the assembly (29:10), with "the greatness and the power and the glory"; Psalm 22:28 says "belongs" and adds "He rules over the nations"; Obadiah 1:21 says "will belong", after "The deliverers will ascend Mount Zion to rule over the mountains of Esau."

rows.title: He rules over all the kingdoms and gives them to whom He wishes

The Law & history: You are the ruler over all
do You not rule over all the kingdoms of the nations?
You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth
The LORD, the God of heaven, who has given me all the kingdoms of the earth
The LORD, the God of heaven, who has given me all the kingdoms of the earth
The Prophets: You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth
I give it to whom I please
He removes kings and establishes them
the God of heaven has given sovereignty, power, strength, and glory
the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes
the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes
as soon as you acknowledge that Heaven rules
the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes
the Most High God rules over the kingdom of mankind, setting over it whom He wishes

rows.alike: Each says God rules over all kingdoms or gives them: "His kingdom rules over all" (Psalm 103:19), "rule over all the kingdoms of the nations" (2 Chronicles 20:6), "God over all the kingdoms of the earth" (2 Kings 19:15; Isaiah 37:16), "the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes" (Daniel 4:17, 4:25, 4:32), "I give it to whom I please" (Jeremiah 27:5).
rows.different: The speakers differ: David (1 Chronicles 29:12), Jehoshaphat, who asks it as a question (2 Chronicles 20:5-6), Hezekiah in prayer (2 Kings 19:15; Isaiah 37:16), and Cyrus king of Persia, of himself: "who has given me all the kingdoms of the earth" (Ezra 1:2). In Jeremiah 27:5-6 the LORD speaks and goes on to name Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; in Daniel the words are "the decree of the watchers" (4:17), Daniel's to Nebuchadnezzar (2:37, 4:25-26) and to Belshazzar, in the words "setting over it whom He wishes" (5:21).

rows.title: Enthroned between the cherubim

The Law & history: the LORD of Hosts, who sits enthroned between the cherubim
the LORD of Hosts, who is enthroned between the cherubim
the ark of God the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim
O LORD, God of Israel, enthroned between the cherubim
Psalms & wisdom: You who sit enthroned between the cherubim, shine forth
He is enthroned above the cherubim; let the earth quake!
The Prophets: O LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim

rows.alike: Each names the LORD as "enthroned between the cherubim" or "above the cherubim".
rows.different: In 1 Samuel 4:4, 2 Samuel 6:2 and 1 Chronicles 13:6 the words come in sentences about the ark ("the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Hosts", "the ark that is called by the Name"); 2 Kings 19:15 and Isaiah 37:16 are Hezekiah's prayer, "between" in Kings and "above" in Isaiah. Psalm 80:1 calls on the "Shepherd of Israel" to "shine forth"; Psalm 99:1 puts it after "The LORD reigns" with "let the earth quake!"

rows.title: The great King over all the earth

The Law & history: the great king, the king of Assyria
the great king, the king of Assyria
Psalms & wisdom: the great King over all the earth!
For God is King of all the earth
Mount Zion, the city of the great King
a great King above all gods
The Prophets: On that day the LORD will become King over all the earth
For I am a great King
the great king, the king of Assyria
the great king, the king of Assyria
Gospels & Acts: or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King

rows.alike: God is called "the great King" (Psalms 47:2, 48:2; Matthew 5:35), "a great King" (Psalm 95:3; Malachi 1:14), and "King over all the earth" (Psalm 47:2; Zechariah 14:9) or "King of all the earth" (Psalm 47:7). Psalm 48:2 and Matthew 5:35 both have "the city of the great King".
rows.different: Psalm 48:2 names the city "Mount Zion", and Matthew 5:35 "Jerusalem", in a saying against swearing oaths. Psalm 95:3 has "above all gods"; Zechariah 14:9 says "On that day" the LORD "will become" King and adds "the LORD alone, and His name alone"; in Malachi 1:14 the LORD says it Himself, "I am a great King", with "My name is to be feared among the nations". 2 Kings 18:19, 18:28 and Isaiah 36:4, 36:13 say "the great king, the king of Assyria"; Hosea 5:13 and 10:6 have "the great king" beside "Assyria".

rows.title: King of the nations

The Prophets: Who would not fear You, O King of nations?
Revelation: Just and true are Your ways, O King of the nations!
Who will not fear You, O Lord, and glorify Your name?

rows.alike: Both call God "King of nations" or "King of the nations" and ask who would not fear Him: "Who would not fear You" (Jeremiah 10:7), "Who will not fear You, O Lord" (Revelation 15:4).
rows.different: Jeremiah 10:7 goes on "among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is none like You"; in Revelation it is "the song of God's servant Moses and of the Lamb" (15:3), with "Just and true are Your ways" (15:3) and "All nations will come and worship before You" (15:4).

rows.title: King of kings and Lord of lords

The Law & history: the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords
Psalms & wisdom: Give thanks to the God of gods
Give thanks to the Lord of lords
The Prophets: Your God is truly the God of gods and Lord of kings
he will speak monstrous things against the God of gods
You, O king, are the king of kings
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings
The letters: 1 Timothy 6:15
the King of kings and Lord of lords
Revelation: He is Lord of lords and King of kings
KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS

rows.alike: The same doubled form recurs: "God of gods and Lord of lords" (Deuteronomy 10:17), "the God of gods" and "the Lord of lords" (Psalm 136:2-3), "the God of gods and Lord of kings" (Daniel 2:47), "the King of kings and Lord of lords" (1 Timothy 6:15), "KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS" (Revelation 19:16).
rows.different: Deuteronomy and Daniel 2:47 have "God of gods", and Daniel "Lord of kings", where 1 Timothy and Revelation have "King of kings"; Revelation 17:14 puts "Lord of lords" first and says it of "the Lamb", and in 19:16 it is "a name written on His robe and on His thigh". In Daniel 2:47 King Nebuchadnezzar says it to Daniel of "Your God". "King of kings" is also said of the kings Artaxerxes (Ezra 7:12) and Nebuchadnezzar (Daniel 2:37; Ezekiel 26:7).

rows.title: The King, the LORD of Hosts

Psalms & wisdom: The LORD of Hosts-He is the King of Glory
O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God
The Prophets: my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts
the LORD, the King and Redeemer of Israel, the LORD of Hosts
declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts
declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts
declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts
to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts
to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts

rows.alike: "the King" stands beside "the LORD of Hosts": "the King, the LORD of Hosts" (Isaiah 6:5; Zechariah 14:16-17), "the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts" (Jeremiah 46:18, 48:15, 51:57), "The LORD of Hosts-He is the King of Glory" (Psalm 24:10).
rows.different: Isaiah says "my eyes have seen the King" and cries "Woe is me"; Isaiah 44:6 adds "Redeemer of Israel"; in Jeremiah "declares the King" comes in the oracles against Egypt, Moab and Babylon (46:18, 48:15, 51:57); Zechariah 14:16-17 has "the survivors from the nations" going up "to worship the King". Psalm 24:10 asks "Who is He, this King of Glory?" and Psalm 84:3 says "my King and my God".

rows.title: The LORD your King

The Law & history: So the LORD became King in Jeshurun
The LORD shall rule over you.
they have rejected Me as their king
even though the LORD your God was your king
Psalms & wisdom: You are my King, O God
the march of my God and King into the sanctuary
Yet God is my King from ancient times
our king to the Holy One of Israel
shout for joy before the LORD, the King
I will exalt You, my God and King
let the children of Zion rejoice in their King
The Prophets: the LORD is our King. It is He who will save us
the Creator of Israel, and your King
Is her King no longer there?
Israel's King, the LORD, is among you

rows.alike: The LORD is named someone's own King, with "your", "our", "my" or "their": "the LORD your God was your king" (1 Samuel 12:12), "my King and my God" (Psalm 5:2), "the LORD is our King" (Isaiah 33:22), "Israel's King, the LORD, is among you" (Zephaniah 3:15).
rows.different: In Judges 8:23 Gideon refuses to rule ("I will not rule over you"), and in 1 Samuel 8:7 and 12:12 the LORD's kingship is set against the people's asking for a king ("we must have a king to rule over us"). The psalms say "my King" in prayer and praise; Isaiah 33:22 has "our Judge", "our lawgiver", "our King"; Jeremiah 8:19 asks "Is her King no longer there?"

rows.title: Reigning on Mount Zion

Psalms & wisdom: I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain
The LORD extends Your mighty scepter from Zion
Rule in the midst of Your enemies.
The Prophets: the LORD of Hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem
Then the LORD will rule over them in Mount Zion from that day and forever
The deliverers will ascend Mount Zion to rule over the mountains of Esau

rows.alike: Zion is named as the place of rule: "My King on Zion" (Psalm 2:6), "Your mighty scepter from Zion" (Psalm 110:2), "reign on Mount Zion" (Isaiah 24:23), "rule over them in Mount Zion" (Micah 4:7), "ascend Mount Zion to rule" (Obadiah 1:21).
rows.different: Who rules differs: in Psalm 2:6 the LORD says "I have installed My King", and in Psalm 110:2 "The LORD extends Your mighty scepter" to the one told to sit at His right hand (110:1); in Isaiah 24:23 and Micah 4:7 it is the LORD who reigns or rules; in Obadiah 1:21 it is "The deliverers". Isaiah adds "before His elders with great glory", and Micah "from that day and forever".

rows.title: The throne of David established forever

The Law & history: Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me, and your throne will be established forever
I will establish his throne forever
I will set him over My house and My kingdom forever, and his throne will be established forever
I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever
I will establish his kingdom forever, if he resolutely carries out My commandments and ordinances
David's throne will remain secure before the LORD forever
I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised your father David
Psalms & wisdom: I will establish your offspring forever and build up your throne for all generations
I will establish his line forever, his throne as long as the heavens endure
his throne before Me like the sun
The LORD swore an oath to David
One of your descendants I will place on your throne.
If your sons keep My covenant
their sons will also sit on your throne forever and ever
The Prophets: He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom
in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David
David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel
Gospels & Acts: The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!
God had promised him on oath that He would place one of his descendants on his throne

rows.alike: Nearly the same words recur, "establish" with "throne" or "kingdom" and "forever": "your throne will be established forever" (2 Samuel 7:16), "I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever" (1 Chronicles 22:10), "I will establish your offspring forever and build up your throne for all generations" (Psalm 89:4). Psalm 132:11 and Acts 2:30 both have an oath and a descendant placed on the throne: "One of your descendants I will place on your throne", "He would place one of his descendants on his throne".
rows.different: Some places add a condition: "if he resolutely carries out My commandments" (1 Chronicles 28:7), "If your sons keep My covenant" (Psalm 132:12), and 1 Kings 9:5 follows a condition set in 9:4. Isaiah 9:7 has "He will reign on the throne of David" and "there will be no end"; in Luke 1:32 the angel tells Mary "The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David"; in Mark 11:10 the crowd cries "the coming kingdom of our father David"; in Acts 2:30 Peter says David "was a prophet and knew" of the oath.

rows.title: Your throne, O God, endures forever

Psalms & wisdom: Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom
Your throne was established long ago; You are from all eternity
the LORD abides forever; He has established His throne for judgment
The LORD has established His throne in heaven
The Prophets: Your throne endures from generation to generation
The letters: Hebrews 1:8
Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom

rows.alike: Psalm 45:6 and Hebrews 1:8 read word for word alike: "Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom". Lamentations 5:19 has "Your throne endures from generation to generation", and Psalms 9:7, 93:2 and 103:19 say His throne is "established".
rows.different: Psalm 45 is recited to the king (45:1); Hebrews 1:8 introduces the same words "But about the Son He says". Lamentations 5:19 is said to "O LORD". Psalm 9:7 has the throne "for judgment", Psalm 93:2 "long ago", and Psalm 103:19 "in heaven".

rows.title: Righteousness and justice the foundation of the throne

Psalms & wisdom: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne
righteousness and justice are His throne's foundation
Endow the king with Your justice, O God, and the son of the king with Your righteousness
a throne is established through righteousness
his throne will be established in righteousness
A king who judges the poor with fairness-his throne will be established forever
Loving devotion and faithfulness preserve a king; by these he maintains his throne
The Prophets: to establish and sustain it with justice and righteousness
A judge seeking justice and hastening righteousness will sit on it in faithfulness
a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule with justice
He will reign wisely as King and will administer justice and righteousness in the land
He will administer justice and righteousness in the land

rows.alike: A throne or a reign is joined to righteousness and justice: "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" (Psalm 89:14), "righteousness and justice are His throne's foundation" (Psalm 97:2), "a throne is established through righteousness" (Proverbs 16:12), "a king will reign in righteousness" (Isaiah 32:1), "administer justice and righteousness in the land" (Jeremiah 23:5; 33:15).
rows.different: In Psalms 89:14 and 97:2 it is God's own throne; Psalm 72:1 asks it for "the king" and "the son of the king"; Proverbs says it of "kings" and "a king", and 20:28 has "Loving devotion and faithfulness" instead. In Isaiah 9:7 it is "the throne of David", in Isaiah 16:5 "the tent of David", and in Jeremiah 23:5 and 33:15 "a righteous Branch" for David.

rows.title: He will rule from sea to sea

Psalms & wisdom: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth
The Prophets: His dominion will extend from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth
People will stagger from sea to sea
from sea to sea and mountain to mountain

rows.alike: The two share the whole span: "from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth".
rows.different: Psalm 72:8 is a prayer, "May he rule", for the king and the king's son named in 72:1; Zechariah 9:10 says "His dominion will extend", after "Then He will proclaim peace to the nations". Amos 8:12 and Micah 7:12 use "from sea to sea" of people wandering or coming.

rows.alike: Psalm 110:1 "Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet" is given in Luke 20:42-43, Acts 2:34-35 and Hebrews 1:13 in the same words, and many places say one "sat down" or is "seated" or "at the right hand of God" (Mark 16:19; Colossians 3:1; Hebrews 10:12).
rows.different: Matthew 22:44 and Mark 12:36 have "until I put Your enemies under Your feet" where the others have "a footstool for Your feet"; Hebrews 10:13 has "He waits for His enemies to be made a footstool". Matthew 26:64 and Mark 14:62 say "the right hand of Power", Luke 22:69 "the power of God", Hebrews 1:3 and 8:1 "the Majesty"; in Acts 7:55-56 Stephen sees Jesus "standing", not sitting. Psalm 16:8 and Acts 2:25 have the speaker say "He is at my right hand", Psalm 109:31 says "He stands at the right hand of the needy one", Bathsheba "sat down at his right hand" beside King Solomon (1 Kings 2:19), and in Matthew 20:21 and Mark 10:37 the request is to "sit at Your right hand" with "the other at Your left".

rows.title: Your kingdom come

Gospels & Acts: Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come.

Revelation: Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of His Christ.

rows.alike: Most join the kingdom to the word "come": "Your kingdom come" (Matthew 6:10; Luke 11:2), "the kingdom of God has come upon you" (Matthew 12:28; Luke 11:20), "until the kingdom of God comes" (Luke 22:18), "Now have come ... the kingdom of our God" (Revelation 12:10).
rows.different: Matthew's prayer adds "Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven"; Matthew 12:28 has "by the Spirit of God" where Luke 11:20 has "by the finger of God". Luke 17:20-21 answers the Pharisees "The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs" and "the kingdom of God is in your midst"; Mark 9:1 has "see the kingdom of God arrive with power" and Matthew 16:28 has "see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom"; Luke 23:42 is the criminal's "when You come into Your kingdom". Revelation 12:10 is "a loud voice in heaven" saying "Now", as "the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down".

rows.title: Given the kingdom; receiving the kingdom

The Prophets: the time came for them to possess the kingdom

rows.alike: The kingdom is given to people or received by them: "to give you the kingdom" (Luke 12:32), "I bestow on you a kingdom" (Luke 22:29), "receive the kingdom of God" (Mark 10:15; Luke 18:17), "we are receiving an unshakable kingdom" (Hebrews 12:28); Daniel 7:22 has "the time came for them to possess the kingdom".
rows.different: In Daniel 7:22 it is "the saints of the Most High", after "the Ancient of Days arrived and pronounced judgment in favor of" them; in Luke 12:32 the "little flock" are told "Do not be afraid"; in Luke 22:29 Jesus bestows it "just as My Father has bestowed one on Me"; Mark 10:15 and Luke 18:17 add "like a little child"; Hebrews 12:28 adds "let us be filled with gratitude".

rows.different: Matthew 25:34 is the King's word to "those on His right", "you who are blessed by My Father"; 1 Corinthians 6:9-10, Galatians 5:21 and Ephesians 5:5 say who will not inherit and list them; 1 Corinthians 15:50 says "flesh and blood cannot", with "nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable"; Ephesians 5:5 has "the kingdom of Christ and of God"; James 2:5 has "the poor of this world" chosen "to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him".

1 Corinthians 4:20
For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.

rows.alike: Each says what the kingdom "is not": "My kingdom is not of this world" (John 18:36), "the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking" (Romans 14:17), "the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk" (1 Corinthians 4:20).
rows.different: John 18:36 is Jesus answering Pilate, who had asked whether He was the King of the Jews (18:33); it says "My kingdom" and adds "if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews"; Romans 14:17 and 1 Corinthians 4:20 say "the kingdom of God" and add what it is: "righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit", "power".

rows.title: The kingdom torn away and given to another

The Law & history: The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you.
The LORD has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor David.
I will tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten tribes.
I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you.
The Prophets: the kingdom has departed from you
your kingdom has been divided and given over to the Medes and Persians
Gospels & Acts: the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit

rows.alike: A kingdom is taken and given to another: "torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor" (1 Samuel 15:28), "tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant" (1 Kings 11:11), "I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten tribes" (1 Kings 11:31), "divided and given over to the Medes and Persians" (Daniel 5:28), "taken away from you and given to a people" (Matthew 21:43).
rows.different: Samuel says it to Saul (1 Samuel 15:28; 28:17, where it is "your neighbor David"); the LORD to Solomon (1 Kings 11:11); Ahijah to Jeroboam, "out of the hand of Solomon" (11:31) and "away from the house of David" (14:8); "a voice came from heaven" to Nebuchadnezzar (Daniel 4:31); Daniel to Belshazzar (5:28). Matthew 21:43 says "the kingdom of God" and "a people who will produce its fruit", and 21:45 says the chief priests and Pharisees knew Jesus was speaking about them.

rows.title: A banquet, a feast, a supper

The Prophets: On this mountain the LORD of Hosts will prepare a lavish banquet for all the peoples
Gospels & Acts: many will come from the east and the west to share the banquet with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven
People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.
The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father's kingdom
until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God
I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God
I will not drink of the fruit of the vine from now on
so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom
Revelation: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.

rows.alike: Eating and drinking at a banquet: "prepare a lavish banquet" (Isaiah 25:6), "share the banquet ... in the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 8:11), "prepared a wedding banquet" (Matthew 22:2), "eat at the feast in the kingdom of God" (Luke 14:15); Luke 14:15 and Revelation 19:9 both begin "Blessed".
rows.different: Isaiah 25:6 has "On this mountain" and "for all the peoples"; Matthew 8:11 has "from the east and the west" and "the kingdom of heaven"; Luke 13:29 has "east and west and north and south" and "the kingdom of God". At the last supper Matthew 26:29 has "with you in My Father's kingdom", Mark 14:25 "in the kingdom of God", and Luke 22:16 "until it is fulfilled". Luke 14:15 is said by "one of those reclining with Him"; Revelation 19:9 names "the marriage supper of the Lamb".

rows.title: The glory of His kingdom

The Law & history: the glorious riches of his kingdom
Psalms & wisdom: They will tell of the glory of Your kingdom and speak of Your might
the glorious splendor of Your kingdom
The Prophets: for the glory of my kingdom
Gospels & Acts: Declare that in Your kingdom one of these two sons of mine may sit at Your right hand
Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory.
The letters: 1 Thessalonians 2:12
who calls you into His own kingdom and glory

rows.alike: "kingdom" and "glory" are joined: "the glory of Your kingdom" (Psalm 145:11), "the glorious splendor of Your kingdom" (Psalm 145:12), "His own kingdom and glory" (1 Thessalonians 2:12); a request to sit at Your right hand is "in Your kingdom" in Matthew 20:21 and "in Your glory" in Mark 10:37.
rows.different: Psalm 145 speaks to God; in Matthew 20:20-21 the mother of Zebedee's sons asks, and in Mark 10:35-37 James and John ask for themselves; 1 Thessalonians 2:12 says God "calls you into" it. Esther 1:4 and Daniel 4:36 use the words of the kingdoms of Xerxes and Nebuchadnezzar.
